headline: Google has released an experimental Mac app that records and summarises meetings entirely on the user's own computer, without sending audio to the cloud.
score_reason: Pool 5 kept: a useful privacy-first tool, but experimental, Mac-only and possibly a showcase for Google's offline models.
importance_line: Mac users who worry about meeting audio leaving their computer get a free offline note-taker, but it is experimental and runs only on Apple Silicon.
summary: TechCrunch reports that Google has released Google AI Edge Foresight, a free experimental Mac app that transcribes meetings and turns users' shorthand notes into fuller ones using an AI model that runs on the computer itself, so it works with no internet connection. Google says audio, files and notes never leave the machine, but TechCrunch suggests the app may be mainly a showcase for Google's offline Gemma models, and it currently runs only on Apple Silicon Macs.
notes: Pool link was The Verge, which credits TechCrunch as the earlier reporter; credited to TechCrunch.
